formulas.scores: sum_h FP32(ReLU(FP32(FP32(dot_int32[h,k] * query_scale[h]) * key_scale[k])) * converted_head_weight[h]); all nonzero terms and sums in this witness are exactly representable in FP32

mechanism: Both prescaled head weights round to the same FP16 subnormal 2^-18. The second key scale remains 257/256, so candidate 1 becomes strictly larger. A positive common scale is order-preserving in real arithmetic but not when inserted before FP16 rounding.
top2048_embedding: Add 2047 copies of candidate 0 with key scale 2 and any remaining keys with zero INT8 entries. The 2047 added scores exceed both candidates in both paths; the final selected candidate changes at the strict top-2048 cutoff.
reproducer:
import struct
f16 = lambda x: struct.unpack("<e", struct.pack("<e", x))[0]
f32 = lambda x: struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<f", x))[0]
a, b, r = 2**-12 * 129/128, 2**-12, 257/256
target = [f32(f16(a)), f32(f16(b) * r)]
prescaled = [f32(f16(f32(a/64))), f32(f16(f32(b/64)) * r)]
assert target[0] > target[1]
assert prescaled[0] < prescaled[1]
print(target, prescaled)
